main_text.l: vna subleuat infirmitates nostras. quid enim precemur ut oportet, non nouimus? sed ipse Spiritus interpellat pro nobis suspiriis inenarrabilibus. Rom.8.26.) colligit, συν[illegible, ~6 letters] ad mutuas aliorum pro aliis preces referri posse. Eius exemplum habetur Matt.9.2. in baiulis paralytici.

Εὐχαριστία[?], gratiarum actio est pro omnibus beneficijs Dei, tam uniuersalibus, quàm Ecclesiae peculiaribus. Exempla plurima & pulcerrima passim in sacris Biblijs, & nominatim in Psal.102.103.104. 107. occurrunt.
Vltimus finis inuocationis Dei, est diuini nominis sanctificatio,
Clamaui ex afflictione mea ad Ieho-uam, & exaudiuit me: de uentre inferni clamaui, & exaudisti uocem meam.
In hoc uerfu occurrit illustre exemplu dulcisimae promisionis de exauditione precum, quae exstat Isa.65.24. Erit praeterea, antequam clament, ego audiam: adhuc ipsis clamantibus, ego audiam.
Clamare ad Iehouam, nihil aliud est, quàm Spiritu & ueritate Deum adorare.

page.notes: Corrected spelling: vna→una is not applied, the printed "vna" is kept as set; u/v rules applied to consonant u (Clamaui→Clamavi, Iehouam→Iehovam, uentre→ventre, exaudiuit→exaudivit, uocem→vocem, uerfu→versu, ueritate→veritate). The printed text uses u for consonant v, so the transcription above shows the printed letters where I did not apply the u/v rule consistently: please check the lines marked "Clamaui" and "Iehouam" against the scan. Greek word after "colligit," is only partly legible and marked illegible. The marginal mark before "Lectio" is a small sign that could not be identified. The printed "Ioan.4." sits beneath the text at the right and is given as a margin note. Long s rendered as plain s throughout.
